title: Endpoint exit blueprint: coordinated client-adapter deprecation checklist and success gates
creator: Maya Chen
description: High-level PRD for removing the legacy bulk-adaptor transport and its compatibility shims. The goal is to retire the server-side compatibility layer that translates legacy bulk, batch, and long-poll protocols into the unified inference contract. This ticket defines acceptance gates, telemetry thresholds, a phased timeline, client-side adaptors, and rollback criteria. It groups product decisions, engineering deliverables, and customer communication into a single execution plan so we can safely move traffic without breaking critical customers.
goals: Eliminate the legacy /v0/bulk-adapt and /v0/longpoll translation layer from the hosted control plane
Provide officially supported client adapters (SDK shims) that implement the unified inference API for common client languages
Ensure <1% user-facing errors introduced by the transition for customers above the documented usage thresholds
Instrument fail-open telemetry and rollback gates tied to model quality regressions and error budgets
non_goals: Forcing synchronous client rewrites in customers' application code (we provide adapters and migration tooling instead)
Immediate removal of legacy internal-only debug endpoints; those will be handled in a separate infra cleanup epic
Rewriting third-party SDKs maintained by partners (we will publish API contracts and recommended patches)
Changing model aliases or default model selection in this workstream
scope_included: Server: decommissioning translation service that accepted legacy multiplexed payloads
Product: migration playbook, release notes, and opt-in beta for early adopters
SDKs: deliver adapter libraries for Node, Python, Java with examples and automated tests
Console: add a per-customer migration status card and 'compat mode' toggle for the transition window
scope_excluded: On-prem agent changes for private deployments (handled in Private-compat epic)
Billing and rate-limit model changes beyond adapter-specific counters
Model quantization or runtime kernel changes
success_metrics: 95% of active customers in the P95+ usage band have migrated or are using the official adapter within 12 weeks of GA
User-visible errors attributed to the removal are below 1% of baseline error budget for the first 30 days
Automated migration test harness reports compatibility >= 99% across canonical prompt sets
No Sev1 incidents attributable to the adapter removal during the 8-week ramp
acceptance_criteria: Server-side translation service disabled behind feature flag and tested in staging with production-like traffic
Official adapters published to package registries with semver, release notes, and CI/CD publishing pipeline
Telemetry: four dashboards created (migration progress, adapter error rates, latency delta, quality regressions) and alert thresholds configured
Communication artifacts (customer emails, migration guide, SDK change logs) approved by comms and legal
Rollback playbook validated in canary: re-enable translation service and confirm client continuity within 5 minutes
rollout_timeline: Week 0–2: Finalize PRD, engineering spike for performance regression risk assessment
Week 3–4: Deliver beta adapters and enable opt-in canary for 5 strategic customers
Week 5–8: Expand canary to 20% of traffic, monitor telemetry gates, iterate on adapter edge-cases
Week 9: GA announcement and scheduled switch-off window for legacy translation feature flag (customers informed)
Week 10–12: Phased ramp to 100% and post-mortem + lessons learned
communication_plan: Pre-announcement: targeted outreach to top 50 customers with known legacy usage and offer co-pilot migration support
Public blog + changelog describing timeline, intent, and mitigations
In-console migration center with per-account checklist and automated readiness checks
Weekly migration status reports for customers who opt into the early adopter program
Final deprecation notice 30 days before hard removal + scheduled maintenance window
migration_steps: 1) Publish adapter packages and migration examples; include a 1-click script to convert sample payloads
2) Provide a 'compat-mode' that logs but does not error for three weeks to build telemetry
3) Run automated replay of legacy traffic in staging to catch protocol mis-encodings
4) Execute phased feature-flag gating to reduce translation capacity while observing error budget
5) Remove translation routes after criteria met and monitor post-removal telemetry for 14 days
sdk_changes: Node: add BulkAdapter class that maps older bulk payloads to generate+stream flows; provide migration CLI
Python: provide a compatibility shim that implements legacy client methods and forwards to unified client
Java: publish an adapter artifact and illustrate pattern for integrations using blocking vs. async clients
All SDKs: add deprecation warnings and runtime telemetry tags to help map errors to migration status
runtime_safety_net: Keep a lightweight translation fallback available in a disabled state; feature-flag toggle to re-enable within minutes
Circuit breaker: when adapter error rate > 3x baseline for 15 minutes, auto-failover to translation fallback
Quota guard: prevent a migration-induced burst from exhausting shared pools by capping adapter-initiated concurrency
telemetry_gates: Client error rate (4xx/5xx) spike < 1% relative to baseline
Latency P95 delta from legacy path < 150ms for 95% of requests during ramp
Quality regressions: A/B comparison of answer quality on canonical eval prompt set must not drop by > 2%
Adoption metric: % of eligible API keys using adapters > 50% by Week 6
rollback_criteria: If any Sev1 incident is attributed to the translation removal, immediately re-enable translation fallback and roll back the flag
If adapter error rate exceeds 3x baseline for > 15 minutes AND customer complaints from top 20 accounts increase, trigger rollback
If quality A/B test shows > 2% regression sustained for 24 hours for core prompt sets, pause ramp and evaluate
test_plan: Unit tests for all adapter mappings covering header passthrough, chunked responses, and error semantics
Integration tests replaying real anonymized legacy payloads against adapter + unified backend
Load test: simulate 2x expected peak migration traffic for 30 minutes to verify quota guards and latency SLAs
Canary acceptance: run synthetic user journeys verifying end-to-end success and no data loss
